title: Finite $\ell$-group representation filtration
statement:
Let $H$ be a finite $r$-group and let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional
$\mathbf F_r[H]$-module. Then $V^H\neq0$, and $V$ has an $H$-stable finite
filtration whose successive quotients are the trivial one-dimensional
representation.

proof.text:
The augmentation ideal of $\mathbf F_r[H]$ is nilpotent, so the fixed subspace
$V^H$ is nonzero; induction on $\dim_{\mathbf F_r}V$ using the exact sequence
$0\to V^H\to V\to V/V^H\to0$ gives the filtration.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite $\ell$-group and $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional
$\mathbf F_\ell[H]$-module. Then $V^H\ne0$ and $V$ has a finite filtration
by $H$-stable subspaces whose successive quotients are the trivial
one-dimensional representation.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
The group algebra augmentation ideal $J\subset\mathbf F_\ell[H]$ is nilpotent:
induct on $|H|$, choose a central subgroup $C$ of order $\ell$, and use
$(c-1)^\ell=c^\ell-1=0$ together with nilpotence for $H/C$. Choose the least
$r$ with $J^rV=0$; then $J^{r-1}V$ is nonzero and fixed by $H$. Select a
one-dimensional fixed subspace and induct on $\dim V$ after quotienting by it.
This fills the future-reference gap in Tag `0A3R`.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $H$ be an $\ell$-group (every element has $\ell$-power order; $H$ need
not be finite) and $V$ a finite-dimensional $\mathbf F_\ell$-linear
representation of $H$, of dimension $n$. If $V\neq0$ then $V^H\ne0$. Moreover
there is a flag $0=F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_n=V$ of
$H$-stable subspaces with $\dim F_i=i$ such that $H$ acts trivially on each
$F_{i+1}/F_i$, i.e. $hx-x\in F_i$ for $h\in H$ and $x\in F_{i+1}$; its
successive quotients are the trivial one-dimensional representation.

proof.text:
The action factors through the image $\bar H$ of $H$ in the finite group
$\operatorname{GL}(V)$, which is a finite $\ell$-group. If $V\neq0$, the
nontrivial $\bar H$-orbits on the finite set $V$ have cardinality a positive
power of $\ell$, so $\#V^H\equiv\#V\equiv0\pmod\ell$; as $0\in V^H$, this
forces $V^H\neq0$. Build the flag inductively: given $F_i$ with $i<n$, the
quotient $V/F_i$ is a nonzero representation of $H$, so it has a nonzero
invariant vector; let $F_{i+1}$ be the preimage of the line it spans. Then
$F_{i+1}$ is $H$-stable of dimension $i+1$ and $H$ acts trivially on
$F_{i+1}/F_i$.
